title: Remote Access#
content:
Copy Markdown

#Local network

This method is ideal for secure and fast access without exposing your server to the internet. Devices must be connected to the same local network (e.g., Wi-Fi or Ethernet).

Close WeebHub if it is running, change the host to 0.0.0.0 in config.toml, and restart WeebHub.

Identify the private IP address of the host machine running WeebHub. Find it by running ipconfig on Windows or ifconfig on Linux/macOS. Note the IP address, usually something like 192.168.1.x.

Access the web interface on other devices by navigating to http://<private-ip>:43211.

WeebHub is unsecured by default

Add a server password to prevent unauthorized access, as passwordless access is still inherently insecure even on local networks.

#Remote access

Methods for remote access are varied and depend on your desired level of security and convenience. Here are a few options:

#VPN

A VPN creates a secure connection to another network over the internet. This method is more secure than port forwarding and allows you to access WeebHub as if you were on the same local network. The only caveat is that you will need to set up the VPN on the server and all client devices. Some options include Wireguard, NordVPN Meshnet, Tailscale, and ZeroTier.

#Port forwarding

Port forwarding allows you to access WeebHub from anywhere on the internet. This method is less secure than local network access and requires you to expose your server to the internet. Learn how to set up port forwarding on your router by following this guide.

#Other methods

There are other, more involved methods to access servers remotely such as reverse proxies. You can read up on these methods and check out guides on how to set them up on your server after deciding which one is best for you.

#Video Playback

You can change which player WeebHub uses for playback in Settings > Video Playback. If you're using external players, make sure they are configured correctly. If you're using Transcoding / Direct Play, make sure it's set up correctly.

General Knowledge

The video playback method is saved per-device.

#Ignore Missing Files

You can ignore missing file notifications for a specific anime series by clicking the Bell button on the anime page.

#Filler Info

Click on the vertical ellipsis button to open the context menu.

Click Metadata then Fetch filler info.

Pitfall

Accurate results are not guaranteed. You can only modify or add filler info via hooks.

#Metadata Parent

AniList typically separates anime specials into their own entries, since AniDB does not, this can lead to missing metadata. You can link these standalone entries to their parent anime series, allowing WeebHub to fetch the correct metadata from AniDB.

Click on the vertical ellipsis button to open the context menu.

Click Metadata and enter the parent anime series AniList ID.

You can also add an offset for AniDB episode numbering.

Pitfall

Accurate results are not guaranteed. You can only modify episode metadata via hooks.

#Tips

#Context menu

Right-clicking on an episode card opens a context menu with useful options.

Add to Playlist: Add the episode to a playlist.

Play Externally: If you're using the built-in player in WeebHub Denshi and you encounter a playback issue, you can quickly open the episode with your external player without updating playback settings.

#Super Update

Local Anime LibraryLibrary Explorer

This feature is provided by the Library Explorer. It allows you to bulk update file names or metadata.

Info

This is intended to make correcting metadata hydration mistakes a breeze.

Renaming: Use Search for and Replace with to update file names.

Metadata update: Check Edit file metadata and add rules to update metadata.

#Metadata Update

The following example shows how to correct the metadata of episodes that were incorrectly marked as Special.

Episode Number
Search for files with an episode number >=5 and decrement=7.

Result: File with episode number 10 becomes 3.


AniDB Episode
Search for files with type=special and replace with an enumeration ${start=1} (1,2,3,4,...).

Result: The second file goes from S9 to 2, the third from S10 to 3, etc.


File Type
Search for files with type=special and replace with Main.

title: Auto Downloader#
content:
Copy Markdown

The Auto Downloader allows WeebHub to automatically download new episodes of your currently watching anime as soon as they are released. It works by periodically checking RSS feeds from your installed torrent providers.

Requirements

You must have at least one torrent provider extension installed and either a torrent client or debrid service configured.

Good to know

The Auto Downloader is designed for new releases only and does not search for old episodes or complete seasons.

#1. Setup

Before creating rules, you need to enable the Auto Downloader in the settings.

Go to Settings > Auto Downloader.

Toggle Enabled.

Select a Default Provider. This provider will be used to search for torrents unless specified otherwise in a rule.

Otherwise, the default provider set in Settings > Torrent Provider will be used.

Set the Interval. This determines how often WeebHub checks for new episodes (minimum 15 minutes).

Download immediately vs Queue

If 'Download episodes immediately' is disabled, found torrents will be added to the queue. This is useful if you want to manually approve matches.

#2. Rules

The Auto Downloader works based on Rules. You need to create a rule for every anime you want to track. A rule tells WeebHub which anime to look for, where to save the files, and what quality to select.

#Creating a rule

You can create rules one by one or in bulk.

#Bulk Creation

The easiest way to get started is to create rules for all the anime you are currently watching.

Click + New Rule and select Multiple series at once.

Add series or click + All Currently Watching or + All Upcoming.

This will create a basic rule for each series using default settings.

#Configuring a rule

When editing a rule, you can fine-tune exactly how WeebHub finds and filters torrents for that specific series.

Destination & Provider

Destination: The folder on your disk where the file will be moved after downloading.

Provider: You can override the global default provider for this specific rule (e.g., use Nyaa for everything, but AnimeTosho for this specific show).

Search Parameters

These settings determine which torrents are considered potential matches.

Comparison Title: WeebHub compares the torrent name to this title.

Most Likely (Default): Uses fuzzy matching. It handles variations and takes AniList synonyms into account.

Exact Match: The torrent name must contain this string exactly. Use this only if "Most Likely" is picking up the wrong show.

Episodes to look for:

Recent releases: Only looks for the next episode based on your current progress (e.g., if you watched ep 5, it looks for ep 6).

Select: Allows you to specify a list of episodes to download (e.g., 1, 2, 3).

Episode number absolute offset:

Use this if the release group uses continuous numbering (e.g., the file is named Episode 26 but it is actually Season 2 Episode 1).

Example: If the file is #13 but it corresponds to Season 2 Episode 1, set the offset to 12.

WeebHub typically handles this automatically, but you can set it manually if needed.

Filtering & Quality

These settings filter out matches that don't meet your quality standards.

Resolutions: Select allowed resolutions (e.g., 1080p, 720p). If empty, any resolution is accepted.

Release Groups: A list of preferred release groups. If specified, WeebHub will restrict downloads to these groups.

Additional Terms: Case-insensitive terms that must be present in the filename. Each term can have comma-separated variations.

Excluded Terms: Case-insensitive terms that must not be present in the filename. Each term can have comma-separated variations.

#3. Profiles

Profiles are not required for basic usage. They are advanced presets that allow you to reuse complex filters across rules and add scoring logic for torrents.

#Conditions

A profile allows you to define Conditions that assign a "score" to a torrent. When multiple torrents match a rule, the one with the highest score is chosen.

Actions (Block vs Score)

Score: Adds or subtracts points from the torrent's total score.

e.g., +10 for "HEVC", -10 for "WebRip".

Block: Instantly rejects the torrent, regardless of its score.

e.g., Block if title contains "CamRip" or "TC".

Require: Instantly rejects torrents that don't contain the specified term.

e.g., Block if title does not contains "HEVC".

Minimum Score Threshold

In the profile settings, you can set a Minimum Score. If a torrent's final score (after adding up all conditions) is below this number, it will be discarded even if it matches the rule.

#Delayed Downloads

Sometimes, a lower-quality release (e.g., worse codecs, bad subs) comes out first, followed by a high-quality one some time later. The Delay feature lets you wait for the better version.

#How it works

Delay: When a match is found, WeebHub will wait X minutes before downloading.

Skip Delay Score: If a torrent is found with a very high score (defined in your Profile), the delay is skipped, and it downloads (or gets queued) immediately.

While an item is delayed, WeebHub will keep checking for better versions. If a better version appears during the countdown (e.g., a release with a higher score), it swaps the pending download.

Warning

If you keep Skip Delay Score at 0, any torrent with a higher score will NOT be delayed. To implement a baseline delay, set a higher value.

Tip

Delayed torrents can be viewed in the 'Queue' tab

#FAQ

#Why isn't it downloading missing episodes?

The Auto Downloader is designed for new releases only (via RSS feeds). It does not search for old episodes or complete seasons. To download missing episodes, use the manual search feature on the anime page.

#The torrent title has the wrong season number?

Some release groups do not include the season number (e.g., "Jujutsu Kaisen - 25" instead of "Season 2 - 01").

WeebHub handles absolute numbering automatically in most cases.

If you still have issues, try using the Episode number absolute offset in the rule settings.

#Can I use Debrid?

Yes. If you have a Debrid provider configured and enabled, enable Use Debrid Service in the Auto Downloader settings.

title: Auto-select#
content:
Copy Markdown

Auto-select is a feature that allows WeebHub to automatically choose the best torrent for you when streaming. By default, it will prioritize torrents with the highest number of seeds for you chosen resolution.

Auto-select is fully customizable:

You can choose which additional providers to search.

You can prioritize release groups and resolutions.

You can filter out bad torrents based on metadata.

#Customization

Go to Settings > Torrent Streaming or Settings > Debrid Service.


Click Customize auto-select under the Auto-select section.

Preferred resolution: A quick way to tell WeebHub to aim for the "Highest" or any other quality available.

Customize auto-select: Click this button to fine-tune exactly how WeebHub ranks and filters torrents.

How it works

When you start a stream with Auto Select, WeebHub searches your default provider, filters out bad results, and sorts the remaining torrents based on your priority lists.

#1. Providers

Select which torrent providers WeebHub should search.

Priority matters: This list is ordered. WeebHub will prioritize results from the provider at the top.

Max 3: You can select up to 3 providers.

#2. Release Preferences

This section controls which release groups and resolutions you prefer.

Release Groups (Ordered): Add your favorite release groups here (e.g., ASW, SubsPlease). If a torrent comes from a group higher on the list, it gets a higher score.

Resolutions (Ordered): Define your specific resolution priority (e.g., 1080p > 720p > 480p).

Exclude Terms: Any torrent containing these terms will be instantly rejected (e.g., CamRip, Cam Rip, Dub, Dubbed). The search is case-insensitive.

#3. Metadata Preferences

Filter torrents based on technical details like language and video quality.

Preferred Languages: Helpful if you need subs/dubs in a specific language (e.g., French, Spanish). You can enforce this by checking Require language match.

Warning

Requiring a language match is not recommended.

Preferred Codecs: Prioritize some codecs over others

Preferred Sources: Prioritize some sources over others (e.g., BluRay > WebRip)

#4. Special Preferences & Thresholds

Multiple Audio/Subtitles: Prefer torrents with multiple audio/subtitle tracks.

Best Releases: This applied to some providers that can mark releases as "Best". Set to "Prefer" to prioritize these torrents.

Batches: "Neutral" means WeebHub treats batches like any other torrent.

Thresholds:
Min Seeders: Useful to avoid dead torrents.

File Size: Useful to avoid small, low-quality files if needed.

title: Built-in Player#
content:
Copy Markdown

#Overview

WeebHub features a powerful built-in media player with advanced subtitle rendering, customizable keyboard shortcuts, and many quality-of-life features for watching anime.

Info

This guide is not for the Transcoding & Direct Play Built-in Player.

#Key Features

Advanced Subtitle Support - High-quality subtitle rendering with ASS format support

Anime4K Support - Real-time sharpening using Anime4K

Subtitle Translation - Real-time subtitle translation using DeepL or OpenAI

Customizable Keyboard Shortcuts - Remap all player controls to your preference

Screenshot Capture - Take screenshots of the current frame

Picture-in-Picture - Watch in a floating window while multitasking

Multiple Audio/Subtitle Tracks - Easy cycling between available tracks

#Keyboard Shortcuts

All keyboard shortcuts are fully customizable.

Open player preferences

Go to the "Keyboard Shortcuts" tab

Click on a shortcut button to record a new key

Press the desired key on your keyboard

Adjust the value for actions with numeric parameters (seek duration, volume increment, etc.)

#Subtitles

#Preferred Languages

Set your preferred subtitle and audio languages to have them automatically selected when available:

Preferred Subtitle Language - e.g., eng,jpn (comma-separated, in order of preference)

Preferred Audio Language - e.g., jpn,eng,kor (comma-separated, in order of preference)

#Ignored Subtitle Names

Specify subtitle track names to ignore during automatic selection. For example, enter sign & songs to avoid automatically selecting sign/song subtitle tracks when your preferred language is available.

#Subtitle Rendering

#SSA/ASS

By default, WeebHub renders subtitles using the SSA/ASS1 format. For online streaming, this is done by converting all non-ASS subtitle tracks to SSA.

1 ASS (Advanced Sub Station Alpha) is a subtitle format typically used by anime fansubs which supports advanced styling and effects.

Pitfall

The SSA/ASS renderer uses a font that does not support all languages' characters by default. If your language is not rendering correctly, you may need to add custom fonts or disable this feature. Check out the guides below.

#Adding Custom Fonts

If subtitles in your language are not rendering correctly (showing boxes or missing characters), you need to add the appropriate font files to WeebHub's data directory.

Step-by-step guide:

Download the required fonts
For other languages: Visit Google Webfonts Helper (Noto Sans fonts are recommended)

Download the font package and extract the .woff2 file


Extract and copy font files

Navigate to WeebHub's data directory

Copy the font file to the assets folder

Open player menu, enable Subtitle Styles and open the Font submenu

Enter the file name in the player preferences

#Use Native Format

Open player preferences and go to the Subtitles tab

Disable Convert Soft Subs to ASS and WeebHub will render the actual subtitle format (SRT, VTT, etc.) using another renderer.

Info

This option is only available for web players (online streaming)

#Subtitle Translation

Warning

This feature is in alpha and may not work as expected.

The built-in player can automatically translate subtitles to your preferred language in real-time.

#Setup

Open player preferences and go to the Translation tab

Turn on Enable Translation

Choose your translation provider:
DeepL - High-quality translation (limited language support)

OpenAI - Wider language support


Select your target language

Enter your API key for the chosen provider

Click "Save"

Note: Reloading the player is required when switching languages or changing the API key.

#Troubleshooting

#Subtitles not displaying correctly

If you're noticing that your language isn't rendering correctly, try adding a custom font or disabling "Convert Soft Subs to ASS" (web players only).

Ensure the subtitle track is enabled (cycle through tracks with the subtitle key)

#Translation not working

Verify your API key is correct

Reload the player after changing translation settings

Check that your target language is supported by your chosen provider

#Keyboard shortcuts not working

Click on the video player to ensure it has focus

Check if the shortcuts are being captured by another application

Try resetting shortcuts to defaults in the preferences

#v3.8

#UI and Performance Improvements

WeebHub Denshi now uses native View Transitions for smoother navigation and a more polished feel.

Animations have also been updated across the app to be more consistent in speed and feel snapper.

Media entry headers have been slightly redesigned to be more compact and less visually noisy.

Route preloading is now enabled by default and configurable in the settings.

Various optimizations have been made to increase loading speed for media pages. In addition to that, route preloading will make navigating to some media pages feel almost instant.

#Improved Torrent Search

Torrent search can now query many providers at once, which makes it easier to compare results without having to switch between providers manually. This should make discovery faster, especially when availability differs across providers.

#Updated Subtitle Translator

The subtitle translator now supports OpenAI-compatible local LLMs, making it possible to use self-hosted models instead of relying only on remote services. Language selection has also been fixed so translation setup behaves more consistently.

VideoCore (the in-app video player) will also now automatically import local subtitle files from the same directory as the video file. For external player links, a new {subtitleUrl} placeholder has been added to make passing local subtitle files easier.

#Denshi Window State

WeebHub Denshi now remembers window position and size between sessions, so the app reopens where you left it.

#Hide Anime Spoilers

The 'Hide Anime Spoilers' plugin has been implemented natively for better performance. This will hide episode titles, descriptions, and thumbnails until you watch the episode. There is also a new /spoilers command in the Command Palette that lets you toggle spoilers on or off for an individual title for convenience.

#Extension Improvements

Many improvements have been made to the extension system, including more APIs for deeper integrations and better security controls. Extensions can now be disabled directly, which is useful when you need to quickly disable a misbehaving extension without uninstalling it.

Plugins also gained more APIs, including ctx.settings to securely manage app settings, ctx.auth to securely manage authentication, and ctx.extensions to securely manage other extensions. To complement that, there is a new Extension Secure Mode setting that shows a prompt when an extension attempts a sensitive action.

#Online Streaming Improvements

Online streaming now uses a new HTTP/1-based video proxy, which helps avoid some transport-related issues.

There is also a new option to automatically cycle through providers until a working one is found. This option automatically appears when a playback issue is detected.

Streaming now lets you delete the previous batch selection, and debrid downloading has been improved to handle more edge cases with providers like TorBox and Real-Debrid.

#Bug Fixes & Other Improvements

qBittorrent: Fixed support for 5.2.x

Cache mode: Queued updates are now deleted on manual mutation

Online streaming: Fixed video source selection

Online streaming: Fixed occasional HTTP/2-related errors

Plugins: Faster reads for $storage and $store

UI: Fixed some UI issues

Auto Downloader: Fixed handling of debrid downloads

Core: Fixed handling of stale cookies

Updated Go to 1.26.2

#v3.7

#Security Improvements

Security has been tightened across the app and server, with a stronger default posture and more explicit controls for deployments.

Breaking Change

Passwordless access is now local-only, meaning you will need to set a password for hosted deployments if you haven't already.

Passwordless access is now local-only by default (future updates will require a password to enable network access)

Electron renderer security has been improved, and additional checks have been added around client identity and the macOS server-side updater

You can also now enable server.securemode = "strict", which reduces the attack surface for public deployments, but disables some features and plugin APIs

Added server.accessAllowlist, server.trustedProxies, and server.externalUrl as options

#Search and Tags

Search now supports tags, making it easier to filter and find content using them. Global search also no longer filters out adult entries, which makes results more consistent with the source data.

#New Plugin APIs

Plugins gained a new set of APIs and hooks, especially around playback, scanning, torrent workflows, and automation. This should make it easier to build deeper integrations without relying on workarounds.

Added VideoCore play methods and skip data manipulation

Added an API to register an episode tab

Added hooks for Auto Downloader and torrent search

Added API methods for Playback, Scanner, Debrid, Torrent Streaming, Torrent Search, and Auto-select

#Other Improvements

Windows now uses the user-default explorer application to open folders

Text inputs on WeebHub Denshi support a right-click context menu

Subtitle parsing for local files is faster in the in-app player

The Denshi player now enters fullscreen with a double click instead of a double right-click.

Internally, Denshi startup no longer depends on a websocket connection, which should make the app more resilient during launch and reconnection scenarios. Internally, Denshi startup no longer depends on a websocket connection, which should make the app more resilient during launch and reconnection scenarios.

#Bug Fixes

Denshi: Fixed blank screen after server reconnection

Playback: Fixed stale data being used for events

Continuity: Fixed potential progress being ignored

Scanner: Fixed unrelated roman numerals being treated as seasons

Video Proxy: Fixed slow non-HLS video proxy

Plugin: Fixed $storage returning stale data

VideoCore: Fixed screenshots with Anime4K

Transcoder: Added a potential fix for some 10-bit NVENC issues

#v3.6

#Paste Magnet Links

You can now paste magnet links anywhere in the app to start streaming or downloading immediately.

#Refactored Transcoder

The transcoder has been refactored from the ground up to be more efficient and stable. This should lead to easier maintenance and improvements in the long run.

Regarding security, the transcoder endpoints are now behind authentication if you have a server password set, leaving them inaccessible to unauthorized users.

#Other Improvements

Manga: Reading position is now saved when the chapter is not completed

Refactored most unit tests, removed outdated tests

WeebHub Denshi: Video playback is paused when app is minimized or hidden

You can now quickly select all episodes from an anime when creating a playlist

#Bug Fixes

Fixed some issues with the Auto Downloader

Fixed some issues with the Schedule Calendar

Fixed some issues with Local Accounts

Fixed some issues with the built-in media player

#Core Updates

Migrated to React 19

Updated dependencies

#v3.5

#New Library Scanner

The library scanner has been completely rewritten with context-aware matching that goes beyond simple fuzzy matching algorithms. It provides generally more accurate results, especially for complex naming conventions and edge cases that previously required manual intervention.

Key Improvements:

Context-Aware Matching: Handles title variations with smarter parsing and comparison logic

Enhanced Accuracy: Better recognition of multi-season anime, movies, and specials

Anime Offline Database: Leverages the Anime Offline Database for better accuracy when matching without AniList collection

Custom Rules: Configure matching and hydration behavior to fit your library structure

#Enhanced Issue Recorder

The Issue Recorder now captures UI interactions, making it much easier to reproduce and diagnose problems.

New Features:

Session Replay: Records UI interactions for accurate issue reproduction

Screenshots: Attach images directly to your recordings

Notes: Add descriptions to help identify problems

Enhanced analysis: Internal tools now include session replays for faster debugging

#VideoCore Player Updates

The built-in WeebHub media player (VideoCore) received some updates.

New Features:

Transcoding/Direct Play: VideoCore is now used for transcoding and direct play playback

Stats for nerds: Press Z to view detailed playback information including file path, codecs, and performance metrics

Character lookup: Press H to quickly look up characters while watching

Updated subtitle renderer: Upgraded LibASS renderer for more performant subtitle rendering

#Interface Improvements

Search navigation: Sidebar search button now redirects to the search page; use S keybind for quick search anywhere

Theming: New toggle to restore blur effects in the UI

Password Security: Password inputs are now masked by default

Denshi Tray: Click the tray icon to toggle window visibility on desktop

#Tech Stack

The entire frontend has been migrated from Next.js to Tanstack Router + Rsbuild/Rspack with huge DX improvements:

10x faster build times

Up to 3x faster hot reloading on complex components

#Update Channels

As of v3.5.2, WeebHub now supports multiple update channels and has a built-in fallback for when the main channel (GitHub) is down.

GitHub (default): Stable releases

WeebHub: Stable releases, faster deployments

WeebHub Canary: Pre-release builds for testing and stable releases

#Other Improvements

Enhanced filename parser for better file recognition

Super Update: Added support for start= enumeration

Scanner: Improved episode normalization when AniList has more episodes than AniDB

Scanner: Automatically refreshes anime collection after scanning

Optimized AniList rate limiting on both frontend and backend

Updated some UI components

Improved VideoCore performance (v3.5.2)

#Bug Fixes

Auto Downloader: Fixed handling of custom episode offsets

Auto-select: Removed year filter for batch searches

Manga: Disabled 'Continue Reading' button when next chapter is unavailable

VideoCore: Fixed previous/next episode keybinds

TorBox: Seeding options are no longer overridden

Added missing Node polyfills

Fixed home carousel items not loading

#v3.4

#New Auto Downloader

The Auto Downloader has been completely rewritten with a more intuitive and powerful system for automating anime downloads.

New Features:

Profiles: Reusable presets with scoring logic and advanced filters
Scoring System: Score torrents based on release groups, codecs, sources, etc.

Delayed Downloads: Wait for better quality releases before downloading


Queue: Torrents that cannot be downloaded (due to errors) will be queued instead of skipped

Per-rule Providers: Override the default provider for specific shows

Options:

Multi-provider Search: Search up to 3 providers with priority ordering

Metadata Filtering: Filter by language, codec, and source

#Other Improvements

Improved UI Performance
Up to 2x reduction in FPS drops on heavy pages.


Shelved Local Files:

They will be restored after refreshing the library without triggering a full re-scan.

#v3.3

#Subtitle Track Translation

Alpha Release

You can now translate subtitle tracks to your native language using providers like DeepL and OpenAI. This is very early and experimental, so expect some rough edges.

#Plugin Webviews

Plugins can now display webviews (standalone iframes) in WeebHub. This allows enhanced customization and integration with external services. Unlike injected scripts, webviews are sandboxed and cannot access the DOM directly, but they can communicate with the main app through a message API, and can even have dedicated screens.

Nakama Cloud Rooms is a new feature that allows you to host watch parties without exposing your server to the internet. Communication between the host and peer instances is done through WeebHub's Rooms API.

WeebHub Denshi's native player (VideoCore) has been ported to online streaming, allowing you access to the full range of features available.

#v3.0

Important

All built-in extensions have been removed. You will need to install the necessary extensions manually from external sources. Refer to the getting started guide.

WeebHub Denshi is a new desktop client for WeebHub. It was built to replace WeebHub Desktop and is now available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Migrate to Denshi

If you were using WeebHub Desktop, you need to manually download WeebHub Denshi to upgrade. After that, you won't have to manually update it anymore.

Why? WeebHub Desktop was built using Tauri, a lightweight Rust-based framework for building cross-platform desktop applications. Tauri is great, but it's not a good fit for video-oriented applications. WeebHub Denshi is based on Electron, though heavier and more memory-intensive, it is much more stable and consistent.

#Native Media Player

WeebHub Denshi comes with an all-new built-in media player that supports more codecs than web browsers, SSA/ASS subtitles, and even GPU-based sharpening with Anime4K.

Good to know: The built-in media player is still a work in progress. More features will be added in the future.

Full support for Nakama

Subtitle delay

Custom shaders

#Home Screen

The home screen replaces the 'My Library' page. It is now a fully customizable screen that allows you to display your media (anime & manga) and more items in a variety of ways.

#Custom Sources

WeebHub is no longer limited to AniList. You can now create your own custom source extensions (in JavaScript) for adding anime and manga series to WeebHub and share them. Refer to the extension documentation for more information.

#Library Explorer

The library explorer is a new feature that allows you to browse your local anime library and manage your media files. You can now quickly and easily identify and solve mismatches, bulk edit metadata and file names, and more.

#Playlists

The playlist system has been completely rewritten. You can now seamlessly transition between different playback methods. Playlists now work with external player links on mobile. It is also now easier to add episodes to playlists from the right-click context menu.

The native MPV and IINA playlist feature is now leveraged for downloaded media files, providing a truly seamless transition between episodes.

#Improvements

New cache layer for zero downtime
All requests are now automatically cached to disk

WeebHub will keep working as usual when AniList is temporarily down


Unmatched files: Integrated search & preview for faster matching

Auto play next episode now works when episode file is selected manually

Files are now selected automatically based on index after the first one is selected manually

Manual file selection is now easier with a redesigned interface


Torrent client: Select files to download from batches

Online Streaming: Previous/Next button

Various bug fixes

#v2.9

#Nakama

Nakama is a new experimental feature that allows communication between WeebHub instances, enabling features like:

Library sharing: Share your anime library with friends and let them stream it.

Watch together: Watch anime together with friends in real-time.

In the simplest terms, Nakama allows a host WeebHub instance to act as a media source or streaming server. Communication is done through HTTP requests from protected endpoints and WebSockets for real-time updates.

Nakama requires the host WeebHub instance to be accessible over the internet, which can be achieved with multiple methods (like port forwarding, reverse proxy, or using a cloud server).

#Server Password

You can now set a password for your WeebHub instance to protect it from unauthorized access.

#Local Account

WeebHub no longer requires an AniList account by default. Instead, it stores everything locally. Some features will still require an AniList account, such as offline mode.

#Manga Local Source

A new built-in extension allows you to read your local manga files (CBZ, ZIP, Images) directly in WeebHub.

#IINA media player

WeebHub now supports the IINA media player on macOS, allowing you to use it for local, torrent, and debrid streaming.

#Enhanced Calendar

The release calendar has been redesigned to provide a better overview of upcoming and past episode releases, including new filtering options.

Plugins are a new type of extension that allow for more in-depth customization and allow addition of new features — all in JavaScript.

Copy Markdown

#Data directory

The data directory contains all files WeebHub uses to function. It represents a single instance of WeebHub. It is automatically created the first time you launch WeebHub.

The default location of this directory varies depending on your operating system and environment variables. (%APPDATA%\WeebHub on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/WeebHub on macOS, etc.)

You can open it from the in-app settings.

#config.toml

WeebHub uses a config.toml file to store its configuration. This file is located in the data directory.

Info

A restart is required for changes to take effect.

## The current version of WeebHub (DO NOT CHANGE)
version = ''

[cache]
## The directory where cached data is stored
dir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/cache'
## The directory where transcode video segments are stored
transcodedir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/cache/transcode'

[database]
## The name of the database
name = 'WeebHub'

[logs]
## The directory where logs are stored
dir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/logs'

[manga]
## The directory where manga chapters are downloaded
downloaddir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/manga'
## The directory used by the local manga provider
localdir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/manga-local'

[offline]
## The directory where offline assets are downloaded
assetdir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/offline/assets'
## The directory where the offline database is stored
dir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/offline'

[server]
## The host to bind the server to
host = '127.0.0.1'
## Whether the server should run in offline mode
offline = false
## The port to bind the server to
port = 43211
## Password for authenticated remote access
password = ''
## Optional passwordless exceptions for specific public hosts or origins
accessAllowlist = []
## Reverse proxies allowed to supply X-Forwarded-* headers
trustedProxies = []
## Canonical public URL used for proxy-aware HTTPS detection
externalURL = ''
## Passwordless boundary mode: '', 'hardened', 'lax', or 'strict'
secureMode = ''
## Whether SEANIME_WORKING_DIR should be the binary path (true) or the system's working directory (false)
usebinarypath = true

[web]
## The directory where custom web assets like background images are stored
assetdir = '$SEANIME_DATA_DIR/assets'

#Server password

If your WeebHub server is reachable from outside your machine, setting server.password is required. This enables normal authenticated remote access and is the safest default for VPS and reverse-proxy setups.

Add the following line to the [server] section of your config.toml file:

config.toml

[server]
password = 'your_password_here'

#Security

#Secure mode

WeebHub supports passwordless access for local use, but the exact boundary depends on server.secureMode. Local desktop use, localhost use, and Denshi are expected to keep working in the default configuration.

Setting

Purpose

Typical use

server.secureMode = ''

Keeps the baseline passwordless boundary.

Default behavior.

server.secureMode = 'hardened'

Restricts passwordless access to loopback and localhost.

Use when passwordless access should stay local-only.

server.secureMode = 'lax'

Disables the baseline passwordless boundary.

Use only if you intentionally want the broadest passwordless behavior.

server.secureMode = 'strict'

Includes the hardened boundary and adds extra trusted-local-only restrictions for sensitive actions.

Use for tighter host-level protections.

#Default mode

With secureMode = '', passwordless /api/** and /events requests are allowed when the request host is localhost, loopback, or a literal private-LAN address. Browser requests with Origin or Referer still need to come from a trusted local-looking origin or an allowlisted origin, and cross-site requests without usable origin metadata are denied.

Practical effect:

http://127.0.0.1:43211 works

http://192.168.1.10:43211 also works in passwordless mode

Passwordless public hostnames do not work unless they are allowlisted or secureMode = 'lax' is used

Warning

The default passwordless mode is convenient, but it is inherently insecure. For hosted deployments, server.password is required.

#Hardened mode

With secureMode = 'hardened', passwordless /api/** and /events only auto-trust loopback and localhost hosts. Literal private-LAN hosts and origins are no longer auto-trusted, while Denshi's origin remains trusted when the server is local.

Practical effect:

http://127.0.0.1:43211 works

http://192.168.1.10:43211 does not work in passwordless mode

Passwordless public access can still work if the public host or origin is explicitly allowlisted

#Strict mode

Warning

Strict mode is very restrictive and may cause some features to not work as expected.

secureMode = 'strict' includes the hardened passwordless boundary and adds extra trusted-local-only restrictions for sensitive actions. This includes areas such as extension management, selected settings and root-path mutations, and some plugin APIs.

This gives stronger protection, but it does not replace the security benefits of using server.password for authenticated access, and it may cause some features to not work in passwordless mode.

Example:

Plugins no longer have access to system bindings, even with permissions

All download operations are now path-restricted to specific directories

You cannot update certain settings like application paths, unless you are on a trusted local host (e.g. ssh into the server)

#accessAllowlist

Use server.accessAllowlist when you intentionally want passwordless exceptions for specific public hosts or origins (which is a rare case). It opens the passwordless /api/** and /events boundary for the hosts or origins you list.

config.toml

[server]
accessAllowlist = ['https://demo.example.com']

Info

server.accessAllowlist does not make a remote caller trusted local. In strict mode, sensitive operations still require a trusted local boundary.

#Reverse proxies

If WeebHub is running behind Nginx, Caddy, Traefik, or another reverse proxy, configure server.trustedProxies and usually server.externalURL.

Setting

Purpose

Typical use

server.trustedProxies

Declares which proxies may supply X-Forwarded-* headers.

Required when WeebHub should trust forwarded client IP, host, or protocol.

server.externalURL

Canonical public URL used for proxy-aware HTTPS detection and request normalization.

Set this when WeebHub is served behind HTTPS.

If you rely on forwarded headers but do not configure server.trustedProxies, WeebHub treats the direct connection as authoritative. If the public site is HTTPS, set server.externalURL so WeebHub can normalize requests correctly.

#Run multiple instances

Running multiple instances of WeebHub is as simple as launching the executable with a different data directory. You can do this by setting the SEANIME_DATA_DIR environment variable or using the --datadir flag.

This is not possible for the desktop app.

Example

## Run a second instance
WeebHub.exe --datadir="C:\Users\nobody\Documents\WeebHubData"

Example

## Run a second instance
./WeebHub --datadir="/Users/nobody/Documents/WeebHubData"

Info

Give each instance a different port in their respective 'config.toml' file if you plan on running them simultaneously.

#DNS over HTTPS

You can use DNS over HTTPS to bypass potential ISP blocks. To do this, add the following to your config.toml file under the [server] section:

config.toml

[server]
dohurl="https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query{?dns}"

#TLS

config.toml

[server.tls]
enabled = true

#Environment variables

Here are the environment variables that WeebHub uses:

#SEANIME_DATA_DIR

The path to the data directory. Launch WeebHub with this environment variable to set the data directory.

#SEANIME_SERVER_HOST

Launch WeebHub with this environment variable to set the server host. This will override the default host set in the config.toml file when launching WeebHub for the first time.

#SEANIME_SERVER_PORT

Launch WeebHub with this environment variable to set the server port. This will override the default port set in the config.toml file when launching WeebHub for the first time.

#SEANIME_WORKING_DIR

If usebinarypath is set to true, this variable will be set to the directory where the executable is located, otherwise it will be set to whatever the system's working directory for the executable is.

#Home Screen

You can customize the home screen by adding and reordering items.

#Color scheme

WeebHub allows you to customize the color scheme of the UI by setting custom colors.

Go to Settings > User interface and enable color settings

Set the background and accent colors to your liking. Be mindful that the background color should be a dark color for better readability.

You can also choose between the predefined color swatches.

#Background and Banner

WeebHub allows you to set a custom background image and banner.

The images you want to use as banners or backgrounds should be placed in a directory which is configurable in your config.toml file. The default path of the asset directory is $SEANIME_DATA_DIR/assets.

Create a directory named assets in your WeebHub data directory.

Place your images in the assets directory

In the UI settings, set the image paths to the relative path of the image in the assets directory.

#Example

📁 path/to/WeebHub/data/dir
    ├── config.toml
    ├── WeebHub.db
    └── 📁 assets               <- New
        ├── 🖼️ banner.jpg
        ├── 🖼️ background.gif
        └── 🖼️ banner-2.gif

Then, set Background image path to background.gif in the UI settings.

#How to change the asset directory

Change the web.assetdir setting in your config.toml file to whatever you want, the path should be absolute. The default directory is $SEANIME_DATA_DIR/assets.

#Custom CSS

Go to Settings > User interface and enter your custom CSS under the Advanced dropdown.

title: Local Anime Library#
content:
Copy Markdown

#1. Scanning

By default, scanning matches shows in your library to shows added to your AniList account. In other words, if you have files from an anime that wasn't added to your AniList account, these files might not get matched correctly.

Example

##### Local library ######

📁 Attack On Titan Season 3
📁 Jujutsu Kaisen
📁 One Piece
📁 One Piece Film Red <- 🧐 Not in AniList
📁 Blue Lock
📁 Sousou No Frieren
📁 Horimiya: Pieces <- 🧐 Only "Horimiya" in AniList
📁 Bungou Stray Dogs Season 5 <- 🧐 Only Season 1-3 in AniList
📁 Black Lagoon <- 🧐 Not in AniList

##### Results ######

✅ Attack On Titan Season 3
✅ Jujutsu Kaisen
✅ One Piece
❌ One Piece Film Red <- Mismatched to "One Piece"
✅ Blue Lock
✅ Sousou No Frieren
✅ Horimiya: Pieces <- Correctly matched, since it is direct sequel of "Horimiya"
❌ Bungou Stray Dogs Season 5 <- Mismatched to "Bungou Stray Dogs Season 3"
❌ Black Lagoon <- Unresolved

#Scan without AniList data

Unchecking Use my Anilist Collection only will make WeebHub use external sources to match your files to anime series. This is useful if you don't want to add media to your AniList account beforehand, but is generally less accurate.

Slow scanning

This will increase the number of API requests and cause rate limiting. Avoid this if you have a large library (100+ anime), and instead add the media to your AniList account manually before scanning.

Example

##### Local library ######

📁 Attack On Titan Season 3
📁 Jujutsu Kaisen
📁 One Piece
📁 One Piece Film Red <- 🧐 Not in AniList
📁 Blue Lock
📁 Sousou No Frieren
📁 Horimiya <- 🧐 Not in AniList
📁 Bungou Stray Dogs Season 5 <- 🧐 Only Season 1-3 in AniList
📁 Black Lagoon <- 🧐 Not in AniList
📁 Shingeki no Kyojin - The Final Season Part 3


##### Results ######

✅ Attack On Titan Season 3
✅ Jujutsu Kaisen
✅ One Piece
✅ One Piece Film Red
✅ Blue Lock
✅ Sousou No Frieren
✅ Black Lagoon
✅ Horimiya
✅ Bungou Stray Dogs Season 5
✅ Black Lagoon
✅ Shingeki no Kyojin - The Final Season Part 3

#Refreshing entries

WeebHub does not automatically refresh your library by default, so you will need to do this manually by clicking theRefresh library button when you add or remove content.

Info

Make sure to lock your files to avoid your metadata changes being overriden.

#Automatic refresh

You can enable automatic refresh in Settings > Local Anime Library.

Note: Automatic refresh may miss some files when downloading batches.

#2. Check Matches

#Mismatches

General Knowledge

Mismatches aren't bugs. The matching algorithm can make mistakes, especially when dealing with complex cases.

Mismatches can occur for several reasons:

You have not added the anime to your AniList account yet and did not uncheck the Use my Anilist lists only option.

The file/folder name is not similar enough to the anime titles listed on AniList.

The scanner cannot accurately determine the season of the episode. (e.g., File uses a title with a season number while AniList doesn't)

The scanner believes the episode is not part of the main series. (e.g., OVAs, Specials, NC)

Tip

You can check the scan summary to know the definitive reason.

Solutions for most of these cases are straightforward:

Add the anime to your AniList account

Manually resolve the mismatches using Resolve unmatched or the Library Explorer

Update file metadata manually OR rename the file/folder to match the anime title

Manually configure the scanner to correctly match certain files

#Library Explorer

You can use the library explorer to:

See which files were matched incorrectly

Quickly unmatch and match files to the correct anime

Update file metadata to the correct episode (It also has bulk editing capabilities)

Update file names in bulk

Quickly ignore certain files

#Scan Summaries

Summaries are another quick way to find mismatches and understand the reason.

#Lock your files

Once you have resolved all mismatches, you can lock your files to avoid your metadata changes being overriden by future scans. Locked files will not be scanned again. This is important for large libraries.

Tip

You can also lock files from the Library Explorer or the "Bulk Actions" menu in the home screen dropdown.

#3. Manage Files

#Bulk Actions

Click on the vertical ellipsis button to open the context menu.

From there, you can download, unmatch or delete some files.

#File Metadata

Episode metadata comes from AniDB (title, air date) and TheTVDB (title, images, descriptions) and is based on the file metadata (episode numbers) assigned by the scanner.

General Knowledge

If the anime isn't on AniDB or mapping fails, episodes won't have metadata.

WeebHub automatically maps your files to specific episodes by correlating AniList IDs with AniDB metadata. If the scanner misidentifies an episode number or file type, you can manually override these values by updating the file metadata.

Tip

You can also bulk edit file metadata from the Library Explorer with Super Update.

#4. Download

#Search

Make sure you have an extension installed.

On the anime page, make sure you're in the 'Library' tab.

Click on the Download button.

What is smart search?

Some extensions support 'smart search' which gives you handy filters so you don't have to type a search query manually.

Tip

You can select multiple torrents before clicking 'Continue'.

Debrid

If you're downloading via Debrid, the files will be downloaded on your computer once they are available on the Debrid service.

#Auto Downloader

WeebHub allows you to automatically download new episodes as they are released. It does this by periodically checking the RSS feed of your chosen extensions for new episodes and downloading them based on the rules you set.

[

Read the full guide here →

](/autodownloader)

#FAQ

#Can I add multiple library folders?

Yes, you can add multiple library folders in the Settings > Local Anime Library page.

#Why doesn't the Auto Downloader download missing episodes?

The Auto Downloader only downloads new episodes. If you want to download missing episodes, you have to manually search for them and download them.

#How do I remove an anime from 'Missing from your library'?

You can remove an anime from 'Missing from your library' by clicking on the bell icon on the anime page.

#Why were the episodes not matched correctly?

The scanner tries to match files to the correct anime only based on the file names and folder structure.. Even if the file name is parsable, it might not closely match the anime title on AniList, leading to mismatches. Refer to Mismatches for more information on how to resolve mismatches.

#How does the scanner work?

The scanner uses the file names and folder structure to match files to anime series. Read more about it here.

title: Troubleshooting#
content:
Copy Markdown

#Issue Recorder

The Issue Recorder is a tool that allows you to record anonymized logs of the app and send them to the developer for troubleshooting.

How to use the issue recorder

Go to the settings page and click on Record an issue

A small window will appear, click on the Start recording button and recreate the issue you want to report. When you're done, click on the Stop recording button, download the file and send it to the developer.

#Log files

How to find the log files.

Reminder

The default location of the data directory depends on your operating system. ("%APPDATA%\Roaming\WeebHub" or "%APPDATA%\WeebHub" on Windows, "~/Library/Application Support/WeebHub" on macOS, etc.)

In the data directory

All logs are stored in the WeebHub data directory, under the logs folder.

In the app

You can also access the logs from the app itself. Go the settings page and click on the Logs tab. The latest log file is displayed at the top.

#Types of logs

Logs are categorized into two types: scanner logs and server logs.

Scanner logs

Scanner logs are created each time you scan/refresh your anime library.

Server logs

Server logs are created each time you launch WeebHub and are continuously written to during the lifetime of the server.

content:
Copy Markdown

#Add extensions

Good to know

The manga 'library' page and home items are based on what series you add to your lists.

Enable manga support in the settings if you haven't already

Navigate to the Manga page to see your manga lists. (Reading, Planning, Completed)

Find manga provider extensions

#Read chapters

#Refresh sources

WeebHub will cache the chapters from online sources for a few days. Local sources are fetched once when the app is launched. Clicking Refresh sources will empty the cache and fetch the latest chapters for all manga entries you're currently reading.

#Fix incorrect matches

If you notice that the chapters aren't correct or are not found, click Manual match to search and select the correct manga entry from the source. This works for both online and local sources.

#Download from online sources

More on the offline feature.

#1. Add to the queue

Select the chapters you want to download

Click on the Download selected chapters button

This will add the chapters to the download queue

Good to know

The download process does not start automatically after adding chapters to the download queue. You need to start it manually.

#2. Download

Click on the Downloads button in top right corner to open the download drawer.

Click Start to start the download process, Stop to pause the download process, Clear all to remove all chapters from the download queue.

Good to know

The download queue will persist even if you restart the server.

#3. Downloaded chapters

Scroll down to see the list of downloaded chapters.

You can delete downloaded chapters by selecting them and clicking on the Delete selected chapters button.

Note: If you want to delete ALL downloaded chapters regardless of the manga, simply delete the contents of the manga directory in your data directory.

Location of downloaded chapters on disk

The downloaded chapters will be saved in a directory that is configurable in your config.toml file (Default is $SEANIME_DATA_DIR/manga)

Example

path/to/data/dir
└── 📁 manga
    ├── 📁 online_150378_to8mbIMM_1
    ├── 📁 online_150378_oWWoK_2
    └── ...

Note: The directory structure is not human-readable and is not meant to be accessed directly. You should use the web interface to manage downloaded chapters. If you want a more readable and reusable directory, opt for local sources.

#Troubleshooting

WeebHub will automatically detect errors during the download process (e.g. network issues, undownloaded pages, etc.) and will mark the chapter as errored. When that happens, you can click on Reset errored chapters, then you can start the download process again.

If the download process won't start, try restarting the server.

Read the terminal logs for more information about the status of the download process and any errors that may have occurred.

#Local sources

WeebHub supports local file sources (ZIP, CBZ, RAR, .jpg, .png). Add the files to the local manga directory and select Local as the source on the manga page.

The default location of the manga directory is $SEANIME_DATA_DIR/manga-local. You can change it in the manga settings.

Note: You need to refresh the sources each time you add or remove files from the library folder.

#Folder structure

Good to know

There is no strict naming convention, WeebHub uses a parser that expects simple use cases.

Archive

path/to/data/dir
└── 📁 Series
        ├── Chapter 1.cbz
        ├── Chapter 2.cbz
        └── ...

Image

path/to/data/dir
└── 📁 Series
        └── 📁 Chapter 1
                ├── 01.jpg
                ├── 02.jpg
                └── ...

title: Mobile & Other Devices#
content:
Copy Markdown

#Watch on mobile

Info

Your WeebHub instance should be made accessible remotely beforehand. Find the guide here

#Downloaded media

You can watch your downloaded media files on in three ways:

External player link: Use an external player link to a open media files with mobile player apps. (Refer to the guide below)

Nakama: Install WeebHub on the destination device and configure Nakama to stream media files.

Web player: Use transcoding/direct play to watch media files in the browser.

#Streaming

You can stream torrents on mobile with the use of an external player link. (Refer to the guide below)

#External player link

External player links allow the WeebHub interface (web/desktop) to open media files on a device where it's not installed (e.g., mobile) using a custom URL scheme supported by media player apps.

Pitfall

Automatic progress tracking doesn't work with external player links.

On the device you want to watch on, install a media player app that supports custom scheme links (most of them do).

Follow the instructions below to set up the external player link for the player app.

Go to the settings page and External Player Link tab.

Paste the custom scheme link for the player app you want to use.

Go to the Video Playback tab and select External player link for either Downloaded media or Torrent streaming or both.

Make sure your browser allows popups.

Play your media files as usual and WeebHub will open the media player app with the file.

#Custom scheme links

Here are some examples of custom scheme links for popular media players. You can find custom URL schemes for other apps by searching online or checking the app's documentation.

Android

VLC

intent://{url}#Intent;package=org.videolan.vlc;type=video;scheme={scheme};end

MX

intent://{url}#Intent;package=com.mxtech.videoplayer.ad;type=video;scheme={scheme};end

MPV

intent://{url}#Intent;package=is.xyz.mpv;type=video;scheme={scheme};end

All

intent://{url}#Intent;action=android.intent.action.VIEW;scheme={scheme};type=video/*;S.title={formattedTitle};end

iOS

Outplayer

outplayer://{url}

Infuse

infuse://x-callback-url/play?url={url}

VLC

vlc-x-callback://x-callback-url/stream?url={url}

macOS

IINA

iina://weblink?url={url}

Info

External player links can also work on PC, though the configuration process is more advanced.

#Watch on another PC

You have two options to watch media files on another PC:

Nakama

Custom scheme links

#Nakama

Nakama makes it easy to stream media files from your PC to another PC where WeebHub is also installed. Follow the guide here to set it up.

#Custom scheme links

Pitfall

Custom scheme links can be difficult to set up and are not guaranteed to work on desktop. Nakama is recommended for streaming media files from your PC to another PC.

Below are some instructions for setting up the external player link for PC, they are not guaranteed to work.

Linux

Create file WeebHub-open in your $PATH (e.g., /usr/local/bin/WeebHub-open):

WeebHub-open

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# bash and not just sh because we are using some bash-specific syntax
# function to decode url in parameter to be able to pass it to media player
function urldecode() { : "${*//+/ }"; echo -e "${_//%/\\x}"; }

if [[ "$1" == "WeebHub:"* ]]; then
    # remove everything before link
    ref=${1#WeebHub://stream?}
    url=$(urldecode "$ref")
    # Both vlc and mpv works just change this line
    vlc "${url}"
else
    xdg-open "$1" # Just open with the default handler
fi

Make it executable:

sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/WeebHub-open

Create $HOME/.local/share/applications/WeebHub-open.desktop:

WeebHub-open.desktop

[Desktop Entry]
Name=WeebHub handler
Comment=Open WeebHub:// links with VLC.
Exec=WeebHub-open %u
TryExec=WeebHub-open
Icon=vlc
Terminal=false
Type=Application
MimeType=x-scheme-handler/WeebHub;
NoDisplay=true

Register the handler:

xdg-mime default WeebHub-open.desktop x-scheme-handler/WeebHub

Set external player link in WeebHub to:

External

WeebHub://stream?{url}

Make sure to enable base64 path in URL in the settings.

Windows (MPV & VLC)

MPV

Create a new openinmpv.reg file with the following content:

Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"mpv\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"mpv\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Chromium]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"mpv\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\mpv]
@="mpv"
"URL Protocol"=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\mpv\DefaultIcon]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\mpv\shell]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\mpv\shell\open]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\mpv\shell\open\command]
@="C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -Command \"& {Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Web;$PARAMS=([System.Web.HTTPUtility]::UrlDecode('%1') -replace '^mpv://' -replace '(https?)//', '$1://'); Start-Process mpv -WindowStyle Hidden -ArgumentList $PARAMS}\""

Double-click the openinmpv.reg file to import it into the registry.

Set mpv://"{url}" as the external player link in WeebHub.

VLC

Create a new PowerShell vlc-url-scheme.ps1 file with the following content:

param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]
    [string]$URL
)

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Web
$ProcessedURL = ([System.Web.HTTPUtility]::UrlDecode($URL) -replace '^vlc://' -replace '(https?)//', '$1://')
$MoreProcessed = [uri]::EscapeUriString($ProcessedURL)
Start-Process vlc "`"$MoreProcessed`""

Save this script to a permanent location (e.g., C:\Path\vlc-url-scheme.ps1).

Create a new openinvlc.reg file with the following content:

Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"vlc\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"vlc\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Chromium]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"vlc\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox]
"AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins"="[{\"protocol\":\"vlc\",\"allowed_origins\":[\"*\"]}]"

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\vlc]
@="vlc"
"URL Protocol"=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\vlc\DefaultIcon]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\vlc\shell]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\vlc\shell\open]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\vlc\shell\open\command]
@="powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -File \"C:\\Path\\vlc-url-scheme.ps1\" \"%1\""

Note: If you did not place the PowerShell script in C:\Path\vlc-url-scheme.ps1, replace the path on the last line with the actual path you saved it.

Double-click the openinvlc.reg file to import it into the registry.

Set vlc://"{url}" as the external player link in WeebHub.

title: Nakama#
content:
Copy Markdown

Nakama allows you to connect multiple WeebHub instances together, whether it's your own instances running on different devices or instances shared with friends.

Use cases:

Connect your local PC to your self-hosted VPS or home server to access your library remotely

Connect multiple devices within the same network (e.g., laptop to desktop)

Share your library and watch anime together with friends

#Connect as a Peer

Whether you're connecting to your own remote instance or a friend's, the process is the same.

Go to Settings > Nakama, enter the Server URL of the WeebHub instance you want to connect to and the passcode set by the host. Click Save, the connection will be established after a few seconds.

Cloud Rooms: The Server URL should be in the format room://<room-id>, shared by the host.

Self-hosted: The Server URL should be the full URL of the host's WeebHub instance (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:43211 for local network or your VPS URL for remote access).

Wait for the host to start a watch party, then join it from the Nakama modal.

#Hosting

#Cloud (Watch Party)

If you only wish to host watch parties and do not want to self-host the sessions, you can use the Cloud Rooms feature which relies on a central server managed by WeebHub.

All you have to do is:

Go to Settings > Nakama, Hosting tab, switch Enable host mode on and set a passcode.

Info

You do not need to set a server password.

Click the Nakama icon in the sidebar, then click Create a Cloud Room.

Share the Host URL and Passcode with your friends so they can connect to it.

Create a watch party and start playing an anime episode (torrent or online streaming).

Pitfall

For privacy and security reasons, Cloud Room watch parties do not support local file and debrid playback. Only torrent and online streaming are supported.

#Self-hosted

Self-hosting is the best option if you want access to all features Nakama provides, including library sharing.

For personal use (connecting your own devices):

Same network: Your instances can communicate directly using local IP addresses (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:43211)

Remote access: Make your server accessible over the internet using a VPN like Tailscale, or port forwarding

For sharing with friends: Your WeebHub instance needs to be accessible over the internet.

Info

The simplest way to make your server accessible over the internet is to use a VPN like Tailscale.

Protect your server with a password to prevent unauthorized access while it's running.

Setup:

Go to the Settings > Nakama, Hosting tab, switch Enable host mode on and set a passcode. The passcode should be different from the server password for added security.

Choose whether you want to share your library with connected peers.

If sharing with friends, share your server URL and Nakama passcode with them so they can connect to it.

#Watch Party

Once all peers are connected, you can create a watch party and wait for peers to join.

Then, start playing an anime episode from whatever source you want.

How playback methods are handled

Local files: Your server will serve the file directly to connected peers. Be mindful of bandwidth usage.

Torrent streaming: Only playback status is sent.

Online streaming: Only playback status is sent.

Debrid streaming: Stream URL and playback status are sent.

#Relay mode

Relay mode turns the host server into a middle man - it will relay the origin's (a chosen peer) position to all other peers.

For downloaded media, only local files on the host can be streamed.

To use relay mode,

For torrent streams, make sure the host has torrent streaming enabled. For debrid streams, make sure the host has debrid streaming enabled with the correct API key.

Connect to your remote host from your local WeebHub instance

Start a watch party from the host WeebHub instance

Still on the host, click the tower icon in the top right corner of watch party section, then promote your local WeebHub instance to origin

Back on your local WeebHub instance, you can now start playback

Info

Note that torrent and debrid streams will take longer to start in relay mode, as the host has to start the stream itself.

#Library sharing

As a host, you can share your anime library with connected peers. This allows them to stream your local anime files.

Go to Settings > Nakama, in the Host tab, enable the option to share the library.

The connected peers will need to also enable the option to consume the host's library in their settings.

Info

Opting to consume a host's library removes the possibility to see your own library.

#Limitations

Real-Debrid

Hosting a Watch Party using debrid streaming may violate Real-Debrid's Terms of Service and risk getting your account banned.

title: Offline mode#
content:
Copy Markdown

Offline mode allows you to use the main features of WeebHub without an internet connection or when AniList is down. It includes metadata and images for anime and manga, progress tracking and list management.

#1. Choose what you want to save

Go to the Offline page.

Click Select media to save and select the series you want to save for offline mode. Then, click Save locally.

Alternatively, you can automatically save all series you're watching/reading. Go to Settings > App and check Save all currently watched/read media for offline use.

#2. Sync local data

Click Sync now, then Update local data to start the syncing process. By default, this has to be done manually.

Automate this step

In Settings > App check Automatically refresh local data to automatically update your local data every 30 minutes.

#3. Use offline mode

To enable offline mode, navigate to the offline page and click on Enable offline mode.

You can now use WeebHub and make local changes.

#4. Going back online

Click on the offline icon in the sidebar, then confirm the action.

Go to the offline page and click Sync now, then Upload local changes to AniList to update your AniList collection with the changes you made offline.

title: #Scanner
content:
Copy Markdown

The scanner is the core component of WeebHub that traverses your local directories, parses file paths, and matches them to your AniList collection. It is designed to be flexible and work with various file naming conventions.

#How it works

Reading: The scanner goes through through your library paths.

Parsing: It parses file paths to extract the title, season, and episode number. It also normalizes titles to facilitate matching.

Matching: It tries to find a matching media in your AniList collection (or from external sources if specified) based on the parsed metadata.

Hydration: Once a match is found, the scanner updates the file's metadata in WeebHub (e.g., episode number, type) based on the AniDB entry of the media.

#Matching

The scanner works best when your files follow standard naming conventions. It considers both the file name and the folder structure.

#Series

File names should include the season number OR be located in a folder with the season number (e.g., Season 1, S1, 2nd Season).

Season

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 Bungou Stray Dogs
    ├── [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs - S05E01.mkv <- ✅ Season 5
    ├── [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs - S05E02.mkv
    └── ...

Season

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs 5th Season (Batch) [BDRIP 1920x1080] <- ✅ Season 5
    ├── [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs - 01.mkv
    ├── [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs - 02.mkv
    └── ...

Absolute

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs (Batch) [BDRIP 1920x1080]
    ├── [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs - 49.mkv                     <- ✅ Season 5
    ├── [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs - 50.mkv                     <- ✅ Season 5
    └── ...

Multiple

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 [WeebHub] Bungou Stray Dogs (Batch) [DUAL][BDRIP 1920x1080]
    ├── 📁 Season 1                                                 <- ✅ Season 1
    │   ├── Bungou Stray Dogs - 05.mkv
    │   └── ...
    ├── 📁 Season 2                                                 <- ✅ Season 2
    │   ├── Bungou Stray Dogs - 05.mkv
    │   └── ...
    ├── 📁 Season 3                                                 <- ✅ Season 3
        ├── Bungou Stray Dogs - 05.mkv
        └── ...

Multiple

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 [WeebHub] Jujutsu Kaisen Season 1-2 (Batch) [DUAL][BDRIP 1920x1080]
    ├── Jujutsu Kaisen - 01.mkv                                 <- ✅ Season 1
    ├── Jujutsu Kaisen - 02.mkv                                 <- ✅ Season 1
    ├── ...
    ├── Jujutsu Kaisen - 25.mkv                                 <- ✅ Season 2
    ├── Jujutsu Kaisen - S02E02.mkv                             <- ✅ Season 2
    └── ...

#Movies

Movies should be placed in their own folder, preferably near the root of the library. Avoid mixing movie files with series episodes in the same folder.

🚫

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 Neon Genesis Evangelion Complete Series
    ├── Neon Genesis Evangelion 01.mkv
    ├── Neon Genesis Evangelion 02.mkv
    ├── ...
    └── 📁 Rebuild Of Evangelion
        ├── Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone.mkv
        └── Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance.mkv

✅

path/to/local/library
├── 📁 Neon Genesis Evangelion Complete Series
│ ├── Neon Genesis Evangelion 01.mkv
│ ├── Neon Genesis Evangelion 02.mkv
│ └── ...
├── 📁 Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone
│   └── Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone.mkv
└── 📁 Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance
    └── Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance.mkv

#Specials

Specials are episodes that are not part of the main series (e.g. OVAs, NCs). WeebHub will parse them using specific patterns so that they do not interfere with main series progress.

Files should be named as follows:

Anime S00E01.mkv
Anime 00x01.mkv
Anime SP01.mkv
Anime Special 01.mkv

Info

If the special has its own entry on AniList, it should be placed in its own folder to ensure it is matched to that specific entry.

#Episode 0

Sometimes AniList might include "Episode 0" as part of the main episode count (e.g. Mushoku Tensei II). In such cases, ensure that your library includes that special with the episode number 0.

path/to/local/library
└── 📁 [WeebHub] Mushoku Tensei II Isekai Ittara Honki Dasu
    ├── [WeebHub] Mushoku Tensei S2 - 00 (1080p).mkv <- Episode 0
    ├── [WeebHub] Mushoku Tensei S2 - 01 (1080p).mkv
    └── ...

#Episode numbers

WeebHub parses episode numbers from file names. The following examples show the correct ways episode numbers should be formatted.

File

Jujutsu Kaisen S02E05.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 05.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 05v2.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 05'.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 05.2.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 02x05.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen S2 - 05.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen S2_5.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 05 Episode title.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 2 - E05.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen 2 - 05 - Episode title.mkv
Jujutsu Kaisen - S0205 - Episode title.mkv
S02E05 - Episode title.mkv

Avoid the following patterns as they will be ignored or misidentified:

Incorrect

Jujutsu Kaisen 5.mkv              <- (Single digit) Will be IGNORED, rename to "05"
Jujutsu Kaisen 2 05.mkv           <- Will be IGNORED
Jujutsu Kaisen 1-5.mkv            <- Considered a range
Jujutsu Kaisen S2-5.mkv           <- Considered a range
Jujutsu Kaisen 5_2.mkv            <- Equivalent to S05E02, avoid versioning with "_"
Jujutsu Kaisen 05x02.mkv          <- Equivalent to S05E02, avoid versioning with "x"

#Troubleshooting matches

If files are not being matched correctly, check the Scan Summary after a scan. It provides details on why certain files were not matched.

Common reasons for mismatches:

Missing from AniList: You have not added the anime to your AniList account yet.

Title mismatch: The file or folder name is not similar enough to the anime titles listed on AniList.

Ambiguous season: The scanner cannot accurately determine the season of the episode (e.g., file denotes "Season 1" but AniList has no seasons).

Special episode: The scanner believes the episode is not part of the main series while it should be.

#Solutions

Add the anime to your AniList planning list.

Manually configure the scanner using Matching Rules or Resolution Rules.

Rename the file or folder to match the AniList title more closely.

#Metadata Hydration

After a file is matched to a media (AniList entry), the scanner performs hydration. This step is responsible for assigning the correct metadata to the file, using the file's parsed data and the media's information.

The hydrator assigns the following metadata:

Episode number: The relative episode number (e.g., 1, 2, 3).

AniDB episode: A string identifier used for tracking (e.g., 1, S1, OP1).

Type: The type of file (Main, Special, NC).

#Process

The hydrator follows a specific logic (in order) to determine this metadata:

Custom rules: It first checks if any Hydration Rules (defined in settings) apply to the file. If so, it uses the rule's output.

NC/Specials detection: It checks if the filename indicates a Creditless (NC) video or a Special (OVA, OAD).

If detected as NC (e.g., "OP1", "ED"), it is marked as NC.

If detected as Special (e.g., "OVA"), it is marked as Special and assigned an episode number (usually 1 unless specified otherwise).

Movies: If the matched media is a Movie, the file is automatically assigned Episode 1.

Episode normalization:

If the file has a standard number (e.g., 05) and it fits within the media's episode count, it is assigned that number.

Absolute numbering: If the file uses an absolute episode number (e.g., 26) but the media is a sequel (e.g., "Season 2" which starts after ep 25), the hydrator will attempt to "normalize" it. It checks the media's relations (prequels) to subtract the previous episode counts.

Example: File Anime - 26.mkv matched to Anime Season 2 (where S1 has 25 eps) -> Hydrated as Episode 1.

#Examples

Absolute numbering

Files that follow a continuous episode count across seasons can be normalized if the media relations are correct.

File: Anime - 26.mkv

Matched Media: Anime Season 2 (Season 1 had 25 episodes)

Result: Episode 1

Movies

Movies are always hydrated as Episode 1.

File: Movie Title.mkv

Matched Media: Movie Title (Format: Movie)

Result: Episode 1

Specials

Files with specific keywords are hydrated as specials.

File: Anime - OVA.mkv

Matched Media: Anime Season 1

Result: Special 1 (AniDB: S1)

NC (Creditless)

Creditless openings and endings are identified by keywords like OP, ED, NC.

File: Anime - OP1.mkv

Matched Media: Anime Season 1

Result: NC (Opening 1)

Episode 0

Episode 0 is preserved (often a special/prologue).

File: Anime - 00.mkv

Matched Media: Anime Season 1

Result: Episode 0 (AniDB: S1)

#Configuration

You can customize the scanner behavior in Settings > Local Anime Library, under the Advanced tab.

#Matching rules

Matching rules rely on Regex to force the scanner to match specific file paths to a specific AniList media ID. This is useful when the auto-matcher consistently fails for a specific series.

path: The regex pattern (Go flavor) to match against the file paths.

mediaId: The AniList media ID to match against.

{
  "matching": {
    "rules": [
      {
        "pattern": "Jujutsu Kaisen",
        "mediaId": 12345
      }
    ]
  }
}

#Hydration rules

Hydration rules allow you to assign metadata (episode number, type) to files using Regex, overriding the defaults.

mediaId: The AniList media ID to apply this rule to (can use pattern instead).

pattern: The regex pattern (Go flavor) to apply this rule to (can use mediaId instead).

files: A list of rules to parse the episode information.

{
  "hydration": {
    "rules": [
      {
        "mediaId": 12345,
        "pattern": "",
        "files": [
          {
            "filename": "Mob Psycho - S01E(\\d+) - (.*)$",
            "isRegex": true,
            "episode": "$1",
            "aniDbEpisode": "$1",
            "type": "main"
          },
          {
            "filename": "Mob Psycho - NC(OP|ED)(\\d+)$",
            "isRegex": true,
            "episode": "$1",
            "type": "nc"
          },
          {
            "filename": "Mob Psycho - Other.mkv",
            "type": "nc"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

#Verbose logging

Enable verbose logging to see detailed information about the scanning process in the logs.

{
  "logs": {
    "verbose": true
  }
}
